description:
Most of us want to connect, but the words we reach for can sometimes push people away.
In this TEDx talk, Xander Peer Keller shares how a simple shift in language can change everything — especially for those of us living with chronic illness. Through humor, story, and lived experience, Xander reveals what not to say to someone with chronic illness — and what we can say instead to create space for honesty, dignity, and real connection. This talk isn’t only about illness. It’s about how to talk to someone who is struggling, how to choose presence over fixing, and how to build relationships rooted in empathy.

Xander Peer Keller is a speaker, coach, and facilitator with heart—drawing on interdependence, creativity, and everyday magic to build worlds where being different doesn’t mean being alone. Living with chronic illness and rooted in years of community practice, Xander shows how care, creativity, and interdependence can change the way we live and work together.

description:
What songs would you select to describe someone for whom the short-form TEDx talk might not be a great fit? George Maurer and Jeff Engholm perform strong contenders. Jazz performances of Guaraldi, Hart & Rodgers, Mose Allison. George Maurer is a Minneapolis-based pianist, arranger, and jazz composer whose work has taken him around the world—from concert halls to long-distance bicycle journeys. He has performed with artists like Eric Clapton and Bruno Mars, created arrangements for major orchestras including the Minnesota Orchestra and Boston Pops, and earned multiple honors such as two McKnight Composer Fellowships. In recent years, George has blended music, travel, and storytelling through bike-powered expeditions that inspire new compositions, a podcast (Tales from a Bicycle Seat), and projects exploring community, place, and climate. Whether at the piano or on the road, his work is rooted in curiosity, connection, and the belief that music lives in shared human stories.

description: In this TEDx talk, Lucas Wang explores how an education system obsessed with grades has quietly shaped a generation that knows how to succeed on paper—but not how to understand themselves. Drawing from decades of experience observing human behavior across cultures, he explains how the spaces we live in influence our subconscious mind—and how our thoughts, in turn, shape who we become.

Blending ancient insights with modern psychological understanding, this talk invites us to look beyond symptoms and outcomes and instead focus on alignment—between mind, environment, and intention. It challenges the idea that life happens to us, suggesting instead that life unfolds through us, based on what we repeatedly think, feel, and experience.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We are surrounded by more food than ever before, yet we are facing a nutritional drought. Why does a traditionally grown vegetable provide more for our bodies than the produce found in modern grocery stores? This talk pulls back the curtain on the institutional food system to reveal how common agricultural practices—from water-soluble phosphorus to anhydrous ammonia—are inadvertently killing the very microbial life necessary for nutrient-dense food.

By exploring the "underground" community of homesteaders, small-scale farmers, and regenerative growers, we learn that the solution isn't found in a consolidated supply chain, but at the ground level of our own backyards. Discover how to identify truly healthy food, why "soil smell" matters, and how to reconnect with a local food system that prioritizes human health over industrial volume. It is a call to move beyond the grocery store and rediscover the life-sustaining power of real, nutrient-dense ingredients. Michelle Cannon is a farmer
title: Starving at the supermarket & hidden crisis of nutrient density | Michelle Cannon | TEDxLake Geneva

Et si l’émotion n’était pas l’opposé de l’intelligence artificielle…
mais la clé pour la rendre véritablement humaine ?

Dans ce TEDx talk, Othman, créateur du concept d’« Emotion Tech », explore un paradoxe central de notre époque :
l’IA devient toujours plus puissante, plus autonome, plus présente dans nos vies mais elle peine encore à comprendre ce qui nous définit le plus profondément : l’émotion.

À travers des exemples concrets, des apports en neurosciences et des cas d’usage réels, Othman introduit l’Emotion Tech comme un nouveau territoire technologique — celui des technologies capables de mesurer, comprendre et intégrer l’émotion humaine dans les systèmes numériques.

Cette conférence aborde notamment :

•⁠  ⁠Pourquoi 95 % de nos décisions sont guidées par l’émotion
•⁠  ⁠Comment l’émotion agit comme un marqueur biologique de la mémoire
•⁠  ⁠Comment l’IA peut aujourd’hui mesurer les émotions en temps réel grâce aux signaux neuro-cognitifs
